findings.title: SQL query uses user-controlled input with string formatting
findings.evidence: The lookup query interpolates user_id directly into the SQL text.
findings.explanation: Building SQL with unvalidated user-controlled values can allow SQL injection and may let an attacker read or alter data outside the intended lookup.
findings.expected_recommendation: Validate the identifier and use a parameterized query so the database driver treats user_id as data rather than SQL.

findings.title: User ID is not validated before use
findings.evidence: The function accepts user_id and uses it without checking type, format, range, or presence.
findings.explanation: Missing validation makes downstream behavior unpredictable and increases the likelihood that invalid or hostile input reaches sensitive code paths.
findings.expected_recommendation: Validate user_id at the boundary, reject invalid values early, and pass only normalized values to the query layer.

findings.title: Broad exception handler hides lookup failures
findings.evidence: The function catches Exception and returns None for every failure.
findings.explanation: Catching all exceptions without preserving or reporting the failure obscures operational issues and can make security-relevant failures look like normal missing data.
findings.expected_recommendation: Catch only expected database errors, handle them explicitly, and report failures through a safe error path without exposing sensitive details.
